items.title: Server-Side Scope Enforcement as Authoritative Boundary
items.description: Ensure Azure Function (gpt_reader.py) independently enforces allowlist scope for environment, database, collection, and artifact access. Enforcement must not rely on Claude prompt discipline.
items.problem_statement: Current design risks treating Claude as the enforcement layer, creating a potential bypass if Claude is manipulated (e.g., prompt injection).
acceptance_criteria: Azure Function validates all scope constraints independent of request origin.
Out-of-scope requests return HTTP 403 regardless of Claude behavior.
Implementation explicitly documents enforcement location inside Azure Function.
Live UAT demonstrates rejection of out-of-scope access.

items.title: Bearer Token Lifecycle Management (Rotation, Expiration, Revocation)
items.description: Define and implement lifecycle controls for GPTReader Bearer token including rotation schedule, expiration policy, and revocation procedure.
items.problem_statement: Token exists but lacks lifecycle governance, increasing risk of long-lived credential compromise.
acceptance_criteria: Token rotation schedule defined and documented.
Revocation procedure documented and executable.
Expired or revoked tokens return HTTP 401.
Secrets stored only in secure runtime configuration.

items.title: Brain Lock TTL and Deadlock Recovery
items.description: Add TTL and recovery mechanism to brain lock (R32) to prevent indefinite lock conditions.
items.problem_statement: Current mutex design can deadlock if the locking process crashes, blocking all future writes.
acceptance_criteria: Lock includes owner, timestamp, and TTL/expiration.
Expired locks are automatically recoverable or explicitly releasable.
Concurrent write protection remains enforced.
Lock acquisition and recovery events are logged.

items.title: Independent Append-Only Audit Logging
items.description: Move audit logging to an independent, append-only store and expand coverage to include Claude operations.
items.problem_statement: Current audit logs are co-located with service logic and do not cover Claude's privileged actions.
acceptance_criteria: Audit logs stored outside gpt_reader.py execution context.
Append-only behavior enforced or documented with compensating controls.
Retention policy defined.
Audit includes GPT reads and Claude operations (sync, manifest updates, lock events).

items.title: Local Disk Source-of-Truth Resilience (Backup and Rollback)
items.description: Introduce backup, versioning, and rollback capability for local disk source-of-truth model.
items.problem_statement: Local disk lacks inherent version history and creates single-machine dependency risk.
acceptance_criteria: Backup mechanism defined and implemented.
Rollback procedure defined for corrupted sync scenarios.
Data loss risk from local failure mitigated.
Clear distinction between working state and recoverable state.

items.title: Manifest Snapshot Freshness Policy
items.description: Define snapshot expiration, freshness thresholds, and refresh triggers.
items.problem_statement: Snapshots may become stale during execution with no defined policy or warning threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Max snapshot age defined.
Soft warning threshold before expiration.
Refresh trigger conditions explicitly defined.
Behavior on stale snapshot documented.

items.title: Health Check Endpoint for GPTReader Service
items.description: Add /health or /ping endpoint for Azure Function to verify availability before assignment execution.
items.problem_statement: No mechanism to detect service availability prior to execution, leading to wasted iterations.
acceptance_criteria: Health endpoint returns service readiness status.
Claude checks health before initiating assignments.
Failure states are clearly communicated.

items.title: Rate Limiting Definition and Enforcement
items.description: Define explicit rate limits and enforce them at the service level.
items.problem_statement: 429 error exists but no defined limits, preventing capacity planning and predictable behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Requests-per-minute limits defined.
Rate limiting enforced at Azure Function or gateway layer.
429 responses include retry guidance.

items.title: Mongo Query Size Estimation Strategy (507 Handling)
items.description: Clarify and optimize how estimated_result is computed for 507 responses.
items.problem_statement: Unclear whether countDocuments or planner estimates are used; naive counting may be expensive.
acceptance_criteria: Estimation strategy documented.
Performance impact of estimation minimized.
Behavior consistent across collections.

items.title: Multi-Cluster Connection String Governance
items.description: Define storage, naming, rotation, and ownership of multiple MongoDB connection strings.
items.problem_statement: Multi-cluster access introduced without operational governance for connection strings.
acceptance_criteria: Connection string storage location defined.
Naming convention established.
Rotation and update procedure documented.
Ownership and responsibility assigned.

records.title: Brand name audit — ChatHealthy.ai everywhere
records.rule: The brand name is ALWAYS 'ChatHealthy.ai' with the .ai suffix. Never 'ChatHealthy' alone. This applies to ALL business artifacts, documentation, code comments, UI text, marketing, and legal documents.
records.scope: All business artifacts in brain/BusinessArtifacts/, Website/, code UI strings, system prompts, welcome messages, legal docs, investor docs
records.description: BRAND-001: audit all artifacts for ChatHealthy.ai (never ChatHealthy alone).
Consent framework feature spec. Two-tier HIPAA flow.

stream_1_unknown_questions.trigger: User asks a question the system cannot answer
flow: System asks: 'May I record your question so we can improve? We would save a de-identified version of this conversation.'
If yes: de-identify chat history ALWAYS (no verbatim option), store question + de-identified history
If no: do not store question or history
Either way: offer follow-up from ChatHealthy team
stream_1_unknown_questions.de_identification: Always. No verbatim option for unknown questions.

stream_2_contact_me.trigger: User wants someone from ChatHealthy to follow up
flow: PHI warning: 'This conversation may contain personal health information. ChatHealthy is not a HIPAA covered entity.'
User chooses: 'Would you like us to save the full verbatim transcript, or would you prefer we de-identify it first?'
If verbatim: store full raw chat history with consent_verbatim=true
If de-identify: run deIdentify, store scrubbed version with consent_verbatim=false, consent_summary=true
If neither: store contact fields only, no history

bugs_found.bug: Sonnet set consent_verbatim=true when user explicitly asked for de-identification
bugs_found.root_cause: System prompt consent instructions not specific enough about mapping user response to consent flags

bugs_found.bug: PII not scrubbed in stored chat history when de-identify was requested
bugs_found.root_cause: consent_verbatim=true overrode de-identification — deIdentify was never called

feature_requests.title: Long-running request timeout with user consent and performance logging
feature_requests.description: When a chat request exceeds a configurable threshold, show a modal asking if the user wants to continue.

behavior.threshold: Configurable from MongoDB or environment variable (e.g., 30s default)
behavior.first_trigger: After threshold elapsed: overlay modal 'This is taking a long time. Do you want to continue?'

options.no_abandon: User clicks No -> request is abandoned, response discarded
options.yes_continue: User clicks Yes -> keep waiting. Ask again at each multiplier of threshold (2x, 3x, etc.)

behavior.repeat: Each multiplier of the timeout threshold re-asks the question

performance_logging.trigger: After request completes (success, abandon, or error) AND after user completes consent path

implementation_notes: Frontend: modal overlay with Yes/No radio buttons
Frontend: AbortController to cancel fetch on abandon
Backend: timeout threshold from env var or admin.config collection
Backend: performance record written after consent path completes

deliverables.task: Performance tuning — end-to-end response time optimization
deliverables.detail: Profile and optimize: startup time (FIPS load 2x, ~120s), provider search latency (BUG-PERF-001, 87s VA), embedding call overhead, MongoDB query patterns, cold start reduction.

After every deploy, run a warmup script that hits /health (waits for 200), then fires a test provider search and specialty query to force FIPS load, MongoDB connection pool init, and OpenAI client init. First real user gets a warm server. Add to all deploy workflows (deploy-findcare-backend.yml, manual deploys).

deliverables.task: Compound vector search indexes — city+embedding, county+embedding, state+embedding
deliverables.detail: Create compound indexes on providers collection: {practice_address.city, embedding}, {county.name, embedding}, {practice_address.state, embedding}. These allow MongoDB Atlas vector search to pre-filter by geography before scoring embeddings, eliminating full-collection scans. Directly addresses BUG-PERF-001 (87s VA search).

deliverables.task: Automated UAT status updates on commit
